I am 63 years old and I have farmed in Ruvuma since I was a boy. My father taught me everything, and I also attended some school, so I can read what is written on the seed packet and the fertilizer bag. This plot is small, only 0.10 hectares, but it is my home garden next to the house where I grow maize with beans intercropped. Because I own this land, I put manure on it every year from my cattle. I cannot buy a whole bag of fertilizer for such a small piece, but last season my neighbor and I shared a bag of urea, and I put about five kilograms on this plot, which helped the maize grow tall. I will do the same this year. I will use improved seed because the hybrid I planted last season gave me bigger cobs than the local seed, as long as I put some fertilizer. I do not use chemicals for pests on maize — we pull weeds by hand, and the rains in Ruvuma are usually enough, so I do not irrigate. My wife and children will help me work this plot, and we do not need to hire anyone because it is small.
